complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The app has one permanent origin, chosen before the first real user.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: A decision plus two documents and a host setting. The weight is that it is irreversible once users exist: the origin owns their storage.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Every push is typechecked, linted, tested and built.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: One workflow file plus branch protection. No application code.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The production build is served from a host, with a preview for every pull request.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Host configuration: caching, headers and rollback. The content-security policy for a Vite SPA is the only fiddly part.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A failure in the field is reported with a readable stack, and without personal data.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: SDK wiring, source maps and payload scrubbing; the no-personal-data rule is the part that needs care.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The team can see which parts of the app are used, without tracking anyone.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: A script and a handful of named events, carrying no identifiers.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Every place has a title, and a shared link previews the board it points at.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Title from the place, plus static metadata and one social image.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The first paint carries only what the first view needs.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Lazy imports, loading surfaces and a size check in CI.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A workspace survives a crash, a mistake, and a browser that clears its storage.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Split into: (1) the snapshot store — serialise the persisted slice, write the ring, prune to 20, tolerate corrupt entries; (2) the schedule (trailing minute and pagehide) and isolation from the live workspace; (3) the restore surface in the workspace panel behind the existing confirmation; (4) tests: ring bounds, restore fidelity, a corrupt entry, a failed write.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: IndexedDB, a ring with pruning, a restore surface behind confirmation, tolerance for corrupt entries, and isolation from the live workspace.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The app says when it cannot save, and asks the browser to keep the workspace.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) the storage adapter that detects and reports a failed write; (2) the banner — appears while failing, clears when safe — and its export action; (3) persist()/estimate() and the workspace-panel read-out; (4) mock-driven tests for each state.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Detecting a rejected write is subtler than it looks: `setItem` can fail at quota, so the adapter must verify. Then a banner state machine, persist()/estimate(), and mocks.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Two tabs show one workspace, and neither silently overwrites the other.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) the revision in the persisted slice and the guard before a write; (2) the BroadcastChannel/storage channel and reconciliation; (3) the stale-tab notice and reload; (4) two-tab tests.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: A revision guard on every write, two tabs kept coherent, and a stale tab that refuses rather than clobbers, without merging view state.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A schema change never replaces someone's workspace with the demo.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) preserve to a backup key before any migration is attempted; (2) refuse-and-explain in the boot path; (3) the download offer; (4) tests for a known, an unknown and a corrupt version.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Small code on the data-loss path: migration must preserve, refuse and offer rather than reseed. High consequence, not high volume.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Every change to an item goes through one write path, and each item carries a revision.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) the write helper and `rev` on Item, optional; (2) move every item mutator onto it, one action at a time, with the suite green after each; (3) the enumeration test that fails if a mutator bypasses the seam; (4) confirm placements do not bump `rev`.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: A mechanical refactor of about twenty mutators and twenty-one write sites that must change nothing, plus an enumeration test to keep the seam honest. Regression risk rather than conceptual difficulty.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A change says who made it.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: A field on the log entry, stamped by the seam, and one row of display.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A person signs in with a code sent to their email, and nothing else is required.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) provider and sending domain — SPF, DKIM, DMARC on a subdomain; (2) the code and link flow with a session; (3) invitations and first-sign-in acceptance; (4) rate limits and spent-code refusal; (5) the optional Google provider, off by default.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: The code is ordinary; the operational surface is not: email deliverability (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), rate limits, invitations, and a provider choice coupled to the database.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The workspace lives on the server, and the browser holds a cache of it.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) schema and reads for boards, lanes, items, placements, edges, links, users, types, tags, objectives and logs; (2) the repository adapter, with the local build still passing; (3) the write path — optimistic apply, revision, refusal; (4) the offline queue — order, once-only, reconnect; (5) live propagation between clients; (6) the first-sign-in import; (7) server schema migrations.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: The largest task in the backlog by an order of magnitude: a schema for nine entity kinds, an API, a repository adapter, optimistic writes with an offline queue, live propagation, the first-sign-in import and server-side migrations.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A backup exists, and someone has restored from it.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Configuration plus a runbook, but the drill is the requirement: a backup nobody has restored is a hope.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: One person holds a card's pen at a time.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) the lock table and the conditional-upsert endpoints; (2) the presence channel and client lock state; (3) acquisition on edit intent, heartbeat, release and expiry; (4) the read-only drawer and the card mark; (5) the bulk rule and the arrangement exclusion; (6) two-client tests, including expiry and a second tab of the same person.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Server-arbitrated leases, a presence channel, client lock state, the read-only drawer, the card mark, the bulk rule and two-client tests, with a UX that must never strand a card.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A refused write keeps the words and says what happened.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Two refusal states, a field that keeps its text, copy and reload, and no automatic retry.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A workspace has members, and a member's role decides what they may do.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) the workspace entity and the scoping change for every table; (2) membership and the invitation acceptance path; (3) the role table and its enforcement at the API; (4) removal, the last-owner guard and tests.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Workspaces scope every entity already in the schema, which is a schema-wide change, plus roles, invitations, removal and escalation guards.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: A board can be shared as a read-only link, and the link can be revoked.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: A signed token, a read-only render, an API guard and revocation.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The flows that make the product work are tested end to end.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) harness, seeded state and CI wiring; (2) drag and drop, WIP cancel/resume, drawer edits, board design, import and export; (3) the two-client lease flow once the server exists.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Six flows, one of which needs the server to exist. The risk is flakiness rather than difficulty.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The app is usable with a keyboard and a screen reader.
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: (1) focus trap and Escape return in the drawer and dialogs; (2) live-region announcements for a drag, a refusal and a warning; (3) keyboard paths — move to lane, set parent, reorder; (4) axe in CI and reduced motion.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Focus traps and announcements are contained; the hard part is a keyboard path for every drag action, which touches the board's whole interaction model.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: The product says what it does with your data, and can delete it.
complexityAnalysis.complexityReasoning: Public pages, a verified deletion across every table, and support with a changelog.
